extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Form paragraphs and MPEP guidance for examining patent applications and formulating rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 (including AIA and pre-AIA provisions), related 35 U.S.C. 103 obviousness guidance, and subject-matter eligibility considerations. Includes templates for rejection wording, conditions for their use, and cross-references to exceptions and procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.08.aia 102(a)(1), Activity Before the Effective Filing Date of Claimed Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: (a)(1) the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: 1. Use only in applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 examined under 35 U.S.C. 102/103 as amended by the AIA. 2. Must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.03.aia and 7.07.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.12.aia 102(a)(2), U.S. Patent, U.S. Patent Application Publication or WIPO Published Application That Names Another Inventor and Has an Earlier Effectively Filed Date
rubrics_metrics.description: (a)(2) the claimed invention was described in a patent issued under section 151, or in an application for patent published or deemed published under section 122(b), in which the patent or application, as the case may be, names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: 1. Use only in applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 examined under the AIA. 2. Must be preceded by 7.03.aia and 7.07.aia and may be preceded by 7.08.aia. 3. Use only if reference is: (a) U.S. patent under 151 with earlier effective filing date; (b) U.S. patent application publication under 122(b) with earlier effective filing date; or (c) WIPO (PCT) publication designating the US with earlier effective filing date. If any of these was published before the effective filing date, it also applies under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.14.aia Pre-AIA 102(g), Priority of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: (g)(1) during the course of an interference conducted under section 135 or section 291, another inventor involved therein establishes ... that before such person’s invention thereof the invention was made by such other inventor and not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed; or (2) before such person’s invention thereof, the invention was made in this country by another inventor who had not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed it. In determining priority consider dates of conception, reduction to practice, and reasonable diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rejection on pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) is appropriate in an application examined under the AIA first-to-file provisions only if the application also contains or contained at any time (1) a claim having an effective filing date before March 16, 2013, or (2) a specific reference under 120, 121, or 365(c) to any patent or application that contains such a claim. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.15.aia Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1)/102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102 [2] as being [3] by [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Use only in AIA applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 and examined under amended 35 U.S.C. 102/103; must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia. Fill brackets with claim numbers, whether (a)(1) or (a)(2), whether '--clearly anticipated--' or '--anticipated--' with explanation, and the prior art relied upon. Preceding paragraphs required: either 7.07.aia and 7.08.aia and 7.12.aia as appropriate, or 7.103. For claims claiming priority to pre-March 16, 2013 applications include form paragraph 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.15.01.aia Provisional Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) - Common Assignee/Common Applicant/Joint Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application. The copending application would constitute prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) if published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) or patented under 35 U.S.C. 151. This provisional rejection is based upon a presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application. [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that subject matter was obtained from the inventor/joint inventor (102(b)(2)(A)); (2) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of a prior public disclosure (102(b)(2)(B)); or (3) statement under 102(b)(2)(C) re common ownership/assignment or joint research agreement. Terminal disclaimer cannot overcome this rejection (In re Bartfeld). Examiner Notes: Use only for AIA-filed applications; must be preceded by 7.03.aia. Copending application must have a common assignee, common applicant (35 U.S.C. 118) or at least one common inventor. If claims would be obvious over the other copending application use 7.21.01.aia. Insert appropriate bracket contents (claim numbers, application number, assignee/applicant/joint inventor, explanation). Under 35 U.S.C. 101 two patents cannot issue on identical subject matter; related form paragraphs (8.30, 8.32, 8.27.aia, 8.33, 8.34-8.39) may be used. For priority to pre-March 16, 2013 applications precede with 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.15.02.aia Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2), Common Assignee/Applicant/Joint Inventor(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being [2] by [3]. The applied reference has a common [4] with the instant application. Based upon the earlier effectively filed date of the reference, it constitutes prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Might be overcome by (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that subject matter was obtained from the inventor/joint inventor (102(b)(2)(A)); (2) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of a prior public disclosure (if same invention not being claimed) (102(b)(2)(B)); or (3) statement under 102(b)(2)(C) (common ownership/assignment or joint research agreement). Examiner Notes: Use only in AIA applications (post-Mar 16, 2013) and must be preceded by 7.03.aia. Reference must be U.S. patent under 151, U.S. patent application publication under 122(b), or WIPO publication with earlier effective filing date. If published before effective filing date, also applies under 102(a)(1). Fill bracket instructions: claim numbers, whether '--clearly anticipated--' or '--anticipated--', prior art, and indicate --assignee--/--applicant--/--joint inventor-- in bracket 4. Must be preceded by 7.12.aia. Related double patenting and claim-distinctness considerations (form paragraphs 8.30-8.39) apply. For priority to pre-Mar 16, 2013 include 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.15.03.aia Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2), No Common Assignee or Inventor(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being [2] by [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Use only in AIA applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 examined under amended 35 U.S.C. 102/103; must be preceded by 7.03.aia. This is used to reject over a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication or WIPO publication with an earlier prior art date under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) where the reference is not required to have a common assignee/inventor. If any of these was published before effective filing date, also applicable under 102(a)(1). Fill bracket contents per instructions (claim numbers, anticipated/clearly anticipated, prior art). Must be preceded by 7.12.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.16.aia Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1), Public Use, On Sale, or Otherwise Publicly Available
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) based upon a public use or sale or other public availability of the invention. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Use only in AIA applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia. Must be preceded either by 7.07.aia and 7.08.aia or by 7.103. In bracket 1 insert claim numbers under rejection. A full explanation of evidence establishing public use, sale, or other public availability must be provided in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.17.aia 102(a)(1) Rejection Using Prior Art Excepted under 102(b)(2)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has provided evidence that the claimed invention and the subject matter disclosed in the prior art reference were owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same entity ... or were developed under a joint research agreement. However, although reference [2] has been excepted as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2), it is still applicable as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) that cannot be excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C). Applicant may rely on exceptions under 102(b)(1)(A) or 102(b)(1)(B) to overcome this rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Use only in AIA applications filed on/after March 16, 2013; must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia. Include this paragraph following 7.20.aia or 7.15.aia where anticipation is based on a reference that was excepted under 102(b)(2)(C) but still qualifies under 102(a)(1). In bracket 1 identify common assignee. In bracket 2 identify the excepted reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.18.aia Rejection, Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) as being [2] by [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Use only for applications/patents being examined under amended 35 U.S.C. 102/103 (preceded by 7.03.aia) and MUST contain or have contained a claim having an effective filing date before March 16, 2013 or a specific reference under 120, 121, or 365(c) containing such a claim. Fill bracket contents: claim numbers, whether '--clearly anticipated--' or '--anticipated--' with explanation, and prior art relied upon. This rejection must be preceded either by 7.14.aia or by 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2104-Requirements of 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: Section heading for requirements of 35 U.S.C. 101 (patentable subject matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section covers barred subject matter (e.g., Atomic Energy Act), patent eligible subject matter including living subject matter, and guidance for subject matter eligibility analysis used by examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2106-Patent Subject Matter Eligibility (Step 1 and Step 2 Analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes Eligibility Step 1: The Four Categories of Statutory Subject Matter; Eligibility Step 2A: Whether a Claim is Directed to a Judicial Exception; Eligibility Step 2B: Whether a Claim Amounts to Significantly More.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections list analysis for abstract ideas, laws of nature/natural phenomena, markedly different characteristics, integration into a practical application, and Step 2B considerations such as improvements to computer/technology, particular machine, transformation, well-understood routine activity, mere instructions to apply an exception, insignificant extra-solution activity, field of use and technological environment, and streamlined analyses where eligibility is self-evident or shows clear improvement to technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2106.04(a) Abstract Ideas and related groupings/examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection addresses abstract ideas: examples of claims that do not recite abstract ideas, abstract idea groupings, and tentative abstract ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examiner guidance and examples to identify abstract ideas vs. non-abstract claims; helps determine whether claim is directed to an abstract idea in Step 2A.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2106.05-Eligibility Step 2B: Whether a Claim Amounts to Significantly More
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 2B considers whether claim limitations provide 'significantly more' than the judicial exception itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subparts specify meaningful limitations including improvements to computer/technology (2106.05(a)), particular machine (2106.05(b)), particular transformation (2106.05(c)), well-understood routine conventional activity (2106.05(d)), other meaningful limitations (2106.05(e)), mere instructions to apply an exception (2106.05(f)), insignificant extra-solution activity (2106.05(g)), and field of use/technological environment (2106.05(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2106.07-Formulating and Supporting Rejections For Lack Of Subject Matter Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for formulating a rejection for lack of subject matter eligibility and related form paragraphs and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes how to write eligibility rejections, form paragraphs for use, evaluating applicant responses, and clarifying the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2111-Claim Interpretation; Broadest Reasonable Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on claim interpretation using the broadest reasonable interpretation standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections cover plain meaning (2111.01), effect of preamble (2111.02), transitional phrases (2111.03), 'Adapted to/for/Wherein/Whereby' and contingent clauses (2111.04), and functional vs nonfunctional descriptive material (2111.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2120-Rejection on Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Section heading addressing rejections based on prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) and (a)(2) and pre-AIA analogues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes subparts: 2120.01 Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) and (a)(2) and pre-AIA 102(a),(b),(e) for printed publications or patents; 2120.02 Rejections under 102(a)(1) or pre-AIA 102(a)/(b) for knowledge by others, public use, or on sale; and related procedural and substantive guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2128-'Printed Publications' as Prior Art and 2128.01-Level of Public Accessibility Required
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of when a printed publication qualifies as prior art, including the level of public accessibility required and date of availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules on what constitutes a printed publication, how public accessibility is determined, and how to determine the effective date when a publication becomes available as a reference (2128.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2131-Anticipation — Application of 35 U.S.C. 102
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102, including multiple reference rejections, genus-species situations, anticipation of ranges, and secondary considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses how a single reference can anticipate a claim, how to treat genus/species disclosures, ranges, and related evidentiary and legal considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2141-Examination Guidelines for Determining Obviousness Under 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on obviousness analysis including scope and content of prior art, differences between prior art and claimed invention, level of ordinary skill in the art, and the legal concept of prima facie obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes examples of basic requirements of a prima facie case (2143), suggestion/motivation to modify (2143.01), reasonable expectation of success (2143.02), consideration that all claim limitations must be considered (2143.03), supporting a rejection under 103 (2144) including reliance on implicit disclosure, scientific theory, common knowledge, precedent, overlapping ranges, equivalence, suitability, and close structural similarity for chemical compounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2150-Examination Guidelines for 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 as Amended by the First Inventor To File Provisions of the AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview and detailed discussion of changes to 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 under the AIA and how to examine applications under the AIA provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes sections on overview of changes (2151), detailed discussion of AIA 102(a) and (b) (2152) including effective filing date, prior art categories, admissions, and determining whether to apply 102(a)(1) or 102(a)(2); guidance on overcoming AIA 102 rejections (2152.06); form paragraphs for use (2152.07).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2154-Provisions Pertaining to Subject Matter in a U.S. Patent or Application Effectively Filed Before the Effective Filing Date of the Claimed Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) 'U.S. Patent Documents' and related issues such as WIPO published applications, determining effective filing dates, and requirement that reference 'names another inventor'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections: 2154.01 Prior Art Under AIA 102(a)(2) 'U.S. Patent Documents' (including 2154.01(a)-(d)), and 2154.02 Prior Art Exceptions under 102(b)(2) to AIA 102(a)(2) (sections (a)-(c) covering inventor-originated disclosure, inventor-originated prior public disclosure, and common ownership/obligation of assignment).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2155-Use of Affidavits or Declarations Under 37 CFR 1.130 To Overcome Prior Art Rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on using affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 to show disclosures were made by inventor/joint inventor or previously publicly disclosed by inventor/joint inventor, or that subject matter was obtained from the inventor, and on enablement and who may file such affidavits/declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections cover showing inventor-originated disclosure (2155.01), showing prior public disclosure by inventor (2155.02), showing disclosure by another who obtained subject matter from inventor (2155.03), enablement issues (2155.04), who may file an affidavit/declaration (2155.05), and situations where affidavit/declaration is not available (2155.06).
